output.answer: No. As of today (November 11, 2026), Anduril Industries is a privately held company — its own investor-relations page states "Anduril is privately owned" and that it offers no opportunities for retail investors to buy its stock, and there is no publicly announced IPO date or stock ticker. It has instead kept raising large private rounds: a $5 billion Series H announced May 13, 2026 (led by Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz) valued it at $61 billion, and an employee share tender launched October 2026 priced it at roughly $90 billion. Co-founder Palmer Luckey has said the company will "definitely" go public someday (possibly within "low single-digit years"), but it has not filed an S-1 or named underwriters, so an IPO remains a future possibility, not a scheduled event.
caveats: An IPO has no announced date; Luckey's own comments ("definitely" go public, possibly within "low single-digit years") are directional only, and the company has not filed an S-1 or named underwriters.

The ~$90 billion valuation comes from an October 2026 employee tender offer (shares at $94.80 each, capped at ~$1.3 billion) reported by Bloomberg/SmartAsset; it is a private-market tender price, not a market-traded value, and tender details were not publicly confirmed by the company.

Reuters reported in July 2026 that Anduril was discussing financing that could value it at roughly $100 billion, but those discussions were described as fluid with no decisions made — treat as potential, not completed.

Third-party funds claiming to offer retail access to "pre-IPO Anduril shares" are flagged by the company itself as very likely scams; any offer not from or through Anduril should be treated with caution.
